# Objective

Labels currently disappear behind popups (context menus, dropdowns, tooltips)
that open **after** the overlay loads — the continuous-mode case (e.g.
label-click → right-click → app opens a context menu). Make the overlay
re-assert topmost z-order on a short timer while it is up, so labels float
above any same-band popup that appears mid-session.

# Root cause

`OverlayView` is `Topmost="True"` (`Views/OverlayView.xaml:10`) and re-asserts
`SetWindowPos(HWND_TOPMOST, SWP_NOACTIVATE)` **once** at load
(`Views/OverlayView.xaml.cs:71`). Within the `ZBID_DESKTOP` topmost band the
most-recently-positioned window wins, so a popup created after load (a new
context menu) lands above the overlay and the overlay never recovers. Toast
notifications are out of scope — they live in `ZBID_IMMERSIVE_NOTIFICATION`,
above all app windows; no app window (topmost / admin / UIAccess) can cover them
([ADeltaX, "Window z-order in Windows 10"](https://blog.adeltax.com/window-z-order-in-windows-10/)).

# Approach (timer, not event-hook)

Add a `DispatcherTimer` (~100 ms) started after the existing one-shot; each tick
re-asserts `HWND_TOPMOST` with `SWP_NOACTIVATE` (never steals activation → the
menu beneath stays open). `SWP_NOACTIVATE` is menu-safe by construction — the
one-shot already relies on it. Stop the timer on close.

Why a timer over `SetWinEventHook`: KISS — no new P/Invoke, no fragile event
filtering, and 100 ms is imperceptible vs. menu-open latency. Cost is negligible:
`SetWindowPos` on an already-topmost window is essentially a no-op.

# Files

- `src/HuntAndPeck/Views/OverlayView.xaml.cs` — cache the HWND as a field,
  extract a `ReassertTopmost()` helper, start/stop a `DispatcherTimer`.

No `.csproj` change (existing file already compiled). No new `App.config` knob
(internal mechanism; YAGNI).

# Risks / non-goals

- Toast notifications, Action Center, Start menu: unreachable (higher z-band).
  Suppress via Focus Assist / Do Not Disturb — out of scope for this change.
- Composition-drawn menus (some Chromium / Electron popups): may still peek
  through; not guaranteed — only HWND-based popups are affected.
- No unit test: pure P/Invoke / windowing behavior, verified by CI compile +
  manual Windows test (consistent with the rest of the overlay code).

# Verification

- CI (`.github/workflows/build.yml`, `windows-latest`) compiles + xUnit green.
- Manual test on the Windows box: continuous mode → trigger → label-click to
  open a context menu → labels stay on top of the menu; menu stays open (not
  dismissed); label-clicking a menu item still fires.
